{"topic":"dsl","source":"app/src/dsl.ts","section":"contents","text":"# parcad DSL reference

The parcad modelling language.

- Millimetres. Every primitive is centred on the origin; place it with
  `.at(x, y, z)`.
- Shapes are values: reusing one reuses the node.
- A script returns one shape, or named bodies, `return { base, lid }`,
  which are measured apart and against each other and never fused.
  Selectors, tags and treatments work inside one body.
- `checks: [...]` beside the bodies is a list of rules the build must
  hold, judged on every build and reported first; see `Check`.
- A shape may be a *surface*: faces with no inside and free edges where it
  ends. It reports area and free edges instead of a volume; booleans,
  fillets, wall thickness and STL refuse it until `.thicken(t)` makes it a
  solid. See `surfaceLoft`.

    const hole = cylinder(3, 40);
    return box(60, 30, 6).cut(hole.at(20, 0, 0), hole.at(-20, 0, 0));

Every name below is a reserved word in a script: a variable called `box` hides the primitive. What the language cannot do, and what to write instead, is the `gaps` topic.

## Contents

This is the index of `dsl`, not the document: 124 entries in the 10 sections below. Call read_docs with `topic: "dsl"` and `section` set to a section name, or to one entry's name. Every section together is the whole document.

### Functions (1 of 3)
brief, note, partParams, importPart, box, sphere, cylinder, torus, revolve, cone, countersink, tapDrill, clearance, counterbore, holeFor, threadedRod, threadedHole, vesaPattern, line2d, inset, spurGearOutline, spurGearPair

### Functions (2 of 3)
hull, extrude, ngon, pipe, loft, sweep, surfaceExtrude, surfaceRevolve, surfaceLoft, surfaceSweep, stitchSurfaces, union, intersect, repeat, grid, polar, around, scriptBudget, simulateReactionDiffusion

### Functions (3 of 3)
outlineCrossings, outlineGaps, build

### Shape methods
Shape.tag, Shape.reference, Shape.printedUp, Shape.material, Shape.translate, Shape.at, Shape.rotate, Shape.mirror, Shape.scale, Shape.offset, Shape.shell, Shape.thicken, Shape.trim, Shape.split, Shape.offsetSurface, Shape.edges, Shape.vertices, Shape.fillet, Shape.chamfer, Shape.expect, Shape.union, Shape.cut, Shape.intersect

### EdgeSelection methods
EdgeSelection.expect, EdgeSelection.fillet, EdgeSelection.chamfer, EdgeSelection.smooth, EdgeSelection.squircle, EdgeSelection.patch

### VertexSelection methods
VertexSelection.expect, VertexSelection.fillet, VertexSelection.chamfer

### Line2d methods
Line2d.direction, Line2d.normal, Line2d.pointAt, Line2d.length, Line2d.offset, Line2d.meet, Line2d.yAt, Line2d.xAt

### Values
METRIC_FASTENERS

### Types (1 of 2)
Vec3, BoolOptions, AxisDirection, EdgeQuery, EdgeSelector, VertexQuery, VertexSelector, EdgeExpectation, Material, FilletOptions, ChamferOptions, Brief, ImportedPart, EdgeSelection, VertexSelection, Shape, SectionPoint, SectionEntry

### Types (2 of 2)
CurveEntry, Fit, ThreadSize, ThreadOptions, Line2d, OutlinePoint, PathPoint, HelixPath, SplinePath, SweepOptions, LoftSection, TrimKeep, CurveOptions, LoftCurve, PolarOptions, ReactionDiffusionOptions, PrintAxis, Part, Check

I built the plate in parcad and saved it as `Mounts/plate-60x40x5-m4`. Both of its checks passed.

![iso view](/tmp/field-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/exports/renders/24db1148689fad2d-512-iso.png)

![top view](/tmp/field-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/exports/renders/24db1148689fad2d-512-top.png)

**Measured:**
- Size: 60 × 40 × 5 mm
- Hole centres: (±24, ±14) mm, which is 6 mm in from each edge
- Hole diameter: 4.5 mm. parcad's `clearance("M4")` returns the ISO 273 normal-fit value. Tell me if you want the close fit (4.3 mm) or coarse fit (4.8 mm) instead.
- Volume 11,682 mm³, watertight, one body

**Print check:** passed. The thinnest wall is 3.75 mm, between the −X edge and the hole at (−24, −14). It is well above the 0.8 mm minimum.

I could not confirm the part is on your parcad screen. `open_project` reported no viewers, so the app may not be open.
